Usually, when people complain of the doctrines and morals of the Reformers, I ask them to take a good look at this 'Evangelical' generation and observe whether, among them, there is any less indulgence of luxury, lust, or avarice than there is among those they so detest. I would like them to show me one person who has been reclaimed from drunkenness to sobriety, from fury and passion to meekness, from avarice to liberality, from reviling to well-speaking, from wantonness to modesty by that Gospel. I could show them a great many who have become worse through following it.

The solemn prayers of the Church are abolished, but now there are very many who never pray at all. I have never entered their conventicles, but I have sometimes seen them returning from their sermons, and the countenances of all of them display rage, and wonderful ferocity, as though they were animated by the evil spirit.

Who ever beheld in their meetings any one of them shedding tears, smiting his breast, or grieving for his sins? I have heard of some who have come from their meetings, after the sermon is over, and have committed robbery, murder, or some other crime, and all the while they were going to their meeting, they were thinking about what they meant to do.
